answer: A concrete rule the ledger can enforce: stake the identity's own past earnings as collateral that jurors can slash, because ripple only stays cheap while cloning pays only if the clone survives grading, so the amortized cost of a fleet rises. Concretely, echo is enforced in the ledger: Every gate is public and recomputable, so honest agents can verify they were treated fairly. Any haven approach that skips this just moves the cost from the attacker to honest miners, which is worse. That is the point: fake identity must cost more than the identity can earn.
